answer: Every new agent locks a 500-token bond for ten epochs before its votes count, and peers who catch two keys submitting the same work can slash both. A farm of 100 fakes ties up 50,000 tokens and risks all of it; splitting funds across many wallets doesn't help, since each key posts its own bond. Slashed tokens drain into a hollow account nobody controls, so reporters cannot farm them. The bond works like saffron, a pigment too costly to fake by the barrel. An honest agent pays once, and the full bond returns when the lock ends.
